title: A faster, more compact inbox, Ignore, and step comments on the code
intent: Four inbox fixes: Done loses its Close window button, going back to the inbox shows the last list at once instead of a multi-second spinner, inbox cards drop the agent line and the progress/flag column, and you can ignore a review someone else picks up on GitHub. Step comments posted to GitHub now sit on the step's code as a line range, like review bots do, instead of in the review text.

chapters.title: Done has no Close window button
chapters.why: The window hides to the tray anyway; Back to inbox is the only way on.

chapters.title: The inbox shows the last list right away
chapters.why: Home remounted with no value and showed 'Checking agent branches…' for the whole scan. useInbox keeps the last result in the renderer, shows it at once and refreshes behind the header spinner. Review state changes (and Done's result) are applied to that remembered list, so a card's tag and button are right before the scan lands; finished reviews drop out.
chapters.risk: Until the new scan lands, cards can be a few seconds stale, e.g. new commits on a branch.
checks: A scan that started before a change (an ignore) is dropped, not shown over it.

chapters.title: The scan itself runs side by side and is shared
chapters.why: Projects and the branches in each are now read with Promise.all instead of one after the other, and two callers asking at once (Home and Done) share one in-flight scan. Ignored branches skip the diff and summary entirely, but stay in the summary cache so bringing one back is cheap. The per-item logic is unchanged apart from that.
chapters.risk: More git processes run at once on a project with many branches.

chapters.title: Ignore a review, and bring it back
chapters.why: Each card has Ignore. The branch goes on the project's ignored list in the store, leaves Waiting for you, the project counts and Done's Next up, and shows in a collapsed Ignored section with Bring back. Picking it again with Review a branch also brings it back, and the branch picker no longer calls an ignored branch 'In your inbox'. Ignoring resets the shared scan so the reload after it can't return the old list.
checks: It stays ignored when the PR gets new commits, until you bring it back.

chapters.title: Compact inbox cards
chapters.why: Cards drop the agent line (Claude Code · n sessions · PR #) and the right column with step progress, walkthrough source and the first flag. The In progress tag and the PR pill already say most of it. Padding and gaps are smaller, a load error moves into the meta row, and the main button has a fixed width so Ignore lines up.
chapters.risk: Flags like 'n changes outside your request' are no longer on the card; they still shape the suggested order and show on the plan.

chapters.title: Step comments go on the code on GitHub
chapters.why: A comment on a whole step had no line, so it went into the review text with the step's file list. stepAnchor now picks the step's first block of changes GitHub has (not untracked or synthetic) and posts the comment on it as a range, start_line to line, capped at 30 lines; a step that only removes code gets the removed lines. The step title stays on top, with the step's other files. If GitHub rejects a range, postReview tries each as its last line before folding everything into the text as before. Without hunks, or with inline off (the PR moved on), step comments still go in the text.
chapters.risk: GitHub returns 422 for the whole review if any one comment can't be placed, so one bad anchor sends every comment through the fallbacks.
checks: The Finish copy says comments go on the code only when there are comments.

chapters.title: Tests
chapters.why: githubReview places a step comment as a range and still folds it with inline off; stepAnchor skips untracked files, caps long blocks, falls back to removed lines; apiComment maps to GitHub's field names.
